world.label: Pencil Supply Chain
world.summary: A continuing chain of specialists makes pencils and supplies shops and customers.

actions.description: Cut cedar and add logs to the logger's stock.
Buy logs from the logger into the acting sawmill's stock.
Saw logs into slats in the acting mill's stock.
Buy slats from the sawmill into the acting lead maker's stock.
Mine graphite and add it to the miner's stock.
Prepare clay and add it to the supplier's stock.
Buy graphite from the miner into the acting lead maker's stock.
Buy clay from the supplier into the acting lead maker's stock.
Mix graphite and clay into leads in the acting lead maker's stock.
Buy leads from the lead maker into the acting factory's stock.
Buy paint from the materials supplier into the acting factory's stock.
Buy erasers from the materials supplier into the acting factory's stock.
Buy brass ferrules from the materials supplier into the acting factory's stock.
Use slats, leads, paint, erasers, and ferrules to make pencils in the acting factory's stock.
Buy boxes from the box supplier into the acting factory's stock.
Pack pencils into boxes in the acting factory's stock.
Load boxed pencils from the factory into the acting carrier's shipment.
Deliver the carrier's shipment to the named shop, arriving after the represented travel rounds.
Sell pencils from the acting shopkeeper's stock to the named customer.
Buy pencils from the named shop into the acting customer's stock.

processes.description: Ongoing renewal of raw logs, graphite, clay, paint, erasers, ferrules, and boxes at their respective sources.
Ongoing arrival of work at the logger, mill, mine, suppliers, lead maker, factory, carrier, shop, and customer.
Count down active carrier shipments and add arrived boxed pencils to the named shop's stock.

mechanics.rationale: Cutting cedar adds logs to the logger's stock, as described.

checks.label: The logger has enough logs in reserve

limits: This does not model a separate forest reserve; existing logs are the only represented source.
tests: A positive quantity no greater than the logger's stock can be cut; a larger quantity is refused.

mechanics.rationale: Buying logs transfers them from the named logger to the sawmill stock.
limits: No price is charged because a purchase price is not represented in the action description as an amount to exchange.
tests: A sawmill can buy no more logs than the logger holds.

mechanics.rationale: Sawing consumes logs and adds slats to the mill's stock.
limits: The represented model does not specify a conversion ratio, so one log yields one slat.
tests: Sawing is refused when the mill lacks the requested logs.
semantic_bindings: quantity is logs consumed and slats produced

mechanics.rationale: Buying slats transfers them from the named sawmill to the lead maker's stock.
limits: No money transfer is modeled.
tests: A lead maker can buy slats only up to the sawmill's stock.

mechanics.rationale: Mining consumes graphite from the miner's represented reserve and adds it to the miner's stock.

checks.label: The miner has enough graphite in reserve

limits: A separate mine reserve is not represented, so the starting stock is treated as the only available source and is not depleted.
tests: Mining a positive quantity adds graphite to the miner's stock.

mechanics.rationale: Preparing clay adds it to the supplier's stock.
limits: No separate clay reserve is represented.
tests: A positive quantity of prepared clay is added to the supplier's stock.

mechanics.rationale: Buying graphite transfers it from the named miner to the lead maker's stock.
limits: No money transfer is modeled.
tests: The lead maker receives the purchased graphite and the miner's stock decreases by the same quantity.

mechanics.rationale: Buying clay transfers it from the named supplier to the lead maker's stock.
limits: No money transfer is modeled.
tests: The lead maker receives no more clay than the supplier holds.

mechanics.rationale: Making leads consumes graphite and clay and adds leads to the maker's stock.
limits: The represented model does not specify a mix ratio, so each lead consumes one graphite and one clay.
tests: Making leads is refused unless the maker has enough of both ingredients.

mechanics.rationale: Buying leads transfers them from the named lead maker to the factory's stock.

checks.label: The lead maker has enough leads

limits: No money transfer is modeled.
tests: The factory receives the leads bought from the lead maker.

mechanics.rationale: Buying paint transfers it from the named materials supplier to the factory's stock.
limits: No money transfer is modeled.
tests: The factory receives no more paint than the supplier holds.

mechanics.rationale: Buying erasers transfers them from the named materials supplier to the factory's stock.
limits: No money transfer is modeled.
tests: The factory receives no more erasers than the supplier holds.

mechanics.rationale: Buying ferrules transfers them from the named materials supplier to the factory's stock.
limits: No money transfer is modeled.
tests: The factory receives no more ferrules than the supplier holds.

mechanics.rationale: Making pencils consumes the named materials and adds pencils to the factory's stock.
limits: The represented model does not specify a component ratio, so one unit of each listed input makes one pencil.
tests: Pencil making is refused if any required input is insufficient.

mechanics.rationale: Buying boxes transfers them from the named box supplier to the factory's stock.
limits: No money transfer is modeled.
tests: The factory receives no more boxes than the supplier holds.

mechanics.rationale: Packing consumes pencils and boxes and adds boxed pencils to the factory's stock.
limits: The represented model does not specify box capacity, so one box holds one quantity unit of pencils.
tests: Packing is refused unless the factory has enough pencils and boxes.
semantic_bindings: quantity is boxed pencil units packed

mechanics.rationale: Loading transfers boxed pencils from the named factory to the carrier's shipment.

checks.label: The factory has enough boxed pencils

limits: Loading is an explicit transfer; the factory and carrier need not be co-located because their represented locations differ.
tests: The carrier's shipment increases only when the factory has the requested boxed pencils.
semantic_bindings: quantity is boxed pencil units loaded

mechanics.rationale: A delivery starts represented travel; arrival transfers shipment goods to the named shop after the specified rounds.

checks.label: The shipment has enough boxed pencils
The carrier is not already travelling

limits: Arrival is not represented by this action's available effect targets; the shipment quantity remains on the carrier. No destination stock is credited.
tests: The action starts a positive-duration delivery only when the carrier has enough goods and is not already travelling.
semantic_bindings: quantity is the intended delivery amount

mechanics.rationale: Selling transfers pencils from the shopkeeper to the named customer's stock.
limits: No price transfer is modeled because the contract requires a fixed one-unit sale for priced exchanges and the action quantity can exceed one.
tests: The customer receives the quantity sold and the shop's stock decreases by the same amount.

mechanics.rationale: Buying pencils transfers them from the named shop to the customer's stock.
limits: No price transfer is modeled because the contract requires a fixed one-unit sale for priced exchanges and the action quantity can exceed one.
tests: A customer can buy only the quantity the named shop has in stock.

processes.rationale: Renewing raw-material stocks prevents the represented gathering steps from permanently exhausting their starting supplies; this uses only represented stock paths.

checks.label: The logger or miner has a raw-material stock below its reserve

processes.rationale: Supplier stock renewal sustains the represented continuing supply role without creating manufactured goods.

checks.label: The supplier's clay stock is below reserve
